## 3. The evidence that moved it




**The Virtual Cell Challenge is launched**
([40578317](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40578317/), *Cell*, 26 June) — framed
in its own title as a Turing test for the virtual cell. Every dating claim this
corpus makes about virtual-cell vocabulary should be measured from here, and note
that the phrase was already in a *Nature Biotechnology* title two months earlier.

**In the same month, the refutation of the thing being launched.**
[40407144](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40407144/) (*Bioinformatics*, 2 June):
**simple controls exceed the best deep learning algorithms for predicting genetic
perturbations.** Perturbation prediction is the challenge's central task. The
corpus later treats "simple baselines match deep models" as a 2026 phenomenon and
reads the July 2026 scaling nulls as the moment the premise broke; the claim was
in print, in a title, three weeks before the challenge that assumed otherwise.
[40434923](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40434923/) says the same thing for
variant effects in the same month: conservation and solvent accessibility are
almost all you need.

**Agentic AI reaches an oncology journal.**
[40481323](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40481323/) (*Nat Cancer*): development
and validation of an autonomous AI agent for clinical decision-making in
oncology. Four months after the first LLM-agent paper, six months before the
immunology journals see one.

**The checkpoint roster turns over completely.** June nominates Siglec-G/10,
CMTM4, STS2, Piezo1, TTLL12, plus PSGL-1 as a phagocytosis checkpoint, TIM-3 and
ENT1 — eight targets, **all preclinical, none with an agent**. Of May's five, one
reappears. The templated block is at 31, near its peak. A field can be
simultaneously at maximum output and producing nothing that will be tested.

## 4. Refutations

### (a) Landing on a tracked thread

[40202509](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40202509/): neutrophil MYO1F is
required for the response to checkpoint blockade.
[40457060](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40457060/): PD-1 receptor deficiency
*enhances* CD30+ Treg function in melanoma — removing the checkpoint strengthens
the suppressive population, which is the mechanism by which anti-PD-1 could make
a subset of patients worse.
[40146036](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40146036/): CD301b+ monocyte-derived
dendritic cells mediate resistance to radiotherapy.

[40482640](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40482640/) (*Cell*): microbiome
mismatches from microbiota transplants produce persistent off-target metabolic
and immunomodulatory effects. Filed against the neuro-immune-microbiome thread,
and directly relevant to the faecal-transplant trials the thread later counts as
supports.

[40335697](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40335697/) (*Nature*): oncogene
aberrations drive medulloblastoma **progression, not initiation** — which moves
the interception window earlier than the events interception has been targeting.

### (b) Method credibility

[40163891](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40163891/) (*Blood*): hallmarks of
T-cell exhaustion and antigen experience are **absent** in multiple myeloma from
diagnosis through maintenance. A negative result against a framework, published
in the disease where the framework is most heavily invoked.

[40578363](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40578363/) (*Immunity*): diet-derived
LPS determines intestinal IgA induction and repertoire **independently of the
microbiota**. It reassigns to diet what a large literature credits to microbes,
which makes it both a method-credibility card and a warning about the
microbiome arm of the neuro-immune thread.

[40240607](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40240607/) (*Nature*): low overlap
between transcription factor DNA binding and regulatory targets.

[40195448](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40195448/) (*Nat Med*): sociodemographic
biases in medical decision making by large language models — title-stated
empirical evidence of failure, in a month whose clinical-AI counterweight is
otherwise governance commentary.
